newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-YOUNG LYON TRAINEE HELLEBUYCK SIGNS FOR ATLETICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YOUNG LYON TRAINEE HELLEBUYCK SIGNS FOR ATLETICO.

text.p: Lyon soccer trainee David Hellebuyck, 17, said on Wednesday he had signed a three-year contract with Atletico Madrid in a move which revived a controversy in France about the transfers of young players.
Hellebuyck, who said he had been approached by the Spanish club after an under-17 international, is the second French player to sign his first professional contract abroad.
The departure of young Paris St Germain striker Nicolas Anelka to Arsenal earlier this season infuriated French soccer authorities.
According to French soccer rules, young players must sign their first professional contract with the club which trained them in order to prevent wealthier clubs luring them away.
But the Bosman ruling, allowing players to move freely within the European Union, made the rule impossible to apply.
"To me this is a betrayal. He only goes there for the money," said Jose Broissart, head of Lyon's training centre.
"Everything sounds exciting. I will be able to improve and the financial and material conditions are good too since I will have a flat of my own," Hellebuyck told Lyon daily Le Progres.
